migration.backup_notice: OxideTerm created a one-time snapshot of your pre-2.0 data. It is a recovery copy, not an automatic rollback.
migration.overview_description: OxideTerm 2 is a full desktop rebuild, not a visual refresh. This short tour covers the changes that affect everyday use.
migration.overview_native_description: Rust and GPUI replace the bundled WebView path for a leaner desktop runtime.
migration.overview_visual_description: Motion, surfaces, dialogs, and full-window backgrounds now follow one native design language.
migration.overview_features_description: Telnet, remote desktop, Host Tools, files, editing, and networking are part of one workspace.
migration.gpui_description: The UI, terminal, and backend now share one Rust process and a GPU-rendered surface, removing the browser bridge from the main data path.
migration.gpui_no_webview_description: The desktop no longer ships a WebView application shell or xterm.js terminal path.
migration.gpui_memory_description: Measured idle memory fell from roughly 300 MB in 1.x to just over 100 MB in the current 2.0 build.
migration.gpui_direct_path_description: Terminal bytes update Rust state directly and GPUI renders it without JSON, WebSocket, or Base64 passes.
migration.gpui_shared_runtime_description: Terminal, SFTP, forwarding, editing, and Host Tools can reuse the same node runtime.
migration.visual_title: Motion and visuals now speak one language
migration.visual_description: The native interface adds purposeful transitions and consistent surface behavior while keeping motion fully under your control.
migration.visual_motion_description: Dialogs, tabs, sidebars, toasts, and popovers now use coordinated transitions.
migration.visual_motion_control_description: Choose a motion profile in Appearance settings; Off removes transition delays entirely.
migration.visual_language_description: Shared spacing, elevation, status, focus, and interaction states make workspace surfaces more consistent.
migration.visual_background_description: Image backgrounds can now extend behind the activity bar, sidebars, tabs, content, and companion panels.
migration.visual_disable_hint: Switch profiles to preview and apply them immediately. You can change this later in Settings → Appearance.
migration.visual_radius_hint: Drag the slider to preview and apply the global corner radius immediately. You can change it later in Settings → Appearance → Layout.
migration.visual_background_hint: Set an image in Settings → Appearance → Background Image. Choose Entire Window there to extend it behind the whole workspace.
migration.features_description: 2.0 expands connection types and host operations while rebuilding performance-sensitive paths such as SFTP.
migration.features_telnet_description: New native session types cover legacy systems and serial devices.
migration.features_remote_description: Remote desktop sessions now live beside terminal and file workflows.
migration.features_host_tools_description: Monitor resources and work with processes, services, logs, ports, packages, containers, schedules, and tmux.
migration.features_sftp_description: Node-level ownership, parallel queues, archive transfer, short-read recovery, better progress accounting, and resumable stages improve file work.
migration.features_reconnect_description: Short network interruptions can recover the original SSH runtime before replacement is attempted.
migration.features_editor_description: Local file management, previews, project trees, safe writes, conflicts, syntax, and workspace restore are integrated.
migration.internal_description: 2.0 rebuilds ownership, security, packaging, plugins, sync, and recovery around clearer boundaries.
migration.internal_ownership_description: Closing one terminal no longer implicitly destroys unrelated SFTP, forwarding, editing, or Host Tools work.
migration.internal_security_description: russh with ring, strict host keys, OS keychain storage, and explicit secret boundaries replace older transport layers.
migration.internal_plugins_description: Native manifests, Wasm, and process runtimes replace the legacy WebView plugin path.
migration.internal_sync_description: Conflict preview, history, rollback, and user-owned storage backends are now part of the workspace.
migration.internal_updates_description: Signed metadata, checksums, platform packages, backup snapshots, and recovery paths support the 2.0 lifecycle.
migration.internal_platform_description: macOS, Windows, and Linux each receive native window, process, input, packaging, and integration handling.
migration.internal_finish_notice: Your migrated data remains local. Review connections, authentication, plugins, cloud sync, and AI provider settings after entering the workspace.

onboarding.subtitle: Native workspace for remote operations
onboarding.project_intro: OxideTerm is a Rust-native desktop client for authorized remote operations. It keeps terminal sessions, file transfer, tunnels, serial devices, remote desktop, sync, and optional AI assistance under local user control without a bundled browser runtime.
onboarding.highlight_performance_desc: Async I/O, GPUI native rendering, zero-copy binary protocol.
onboarding.highlight_security_arch_desc: OS keychain, ChaCha20 encryption, pure Rust SSH stack.
onboarding.highlight_crossplatform_desc: macOS, Windows, and Linux with a native look and feel.
onboarding.highlight_extensible_desc: Plugin system, custom themes, MCP integration, CLI tool.

remote_desktop.vnc_anonymous_tls_description: The connection is encrypted, but anonymous TLS cannot prove which server you reached. Continue only if you trust this endpoint and network.
remote_desktop.vnc_legacy_security_description: This security method does not protect the server identity and may expose the session to interception. Continue only on a trusted, protected network.
